## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

AlwaysOnDisplayController — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/display/AlwaysOnDisplayController.kt

## Trigger

A wrist raise, a screen touch, or the transition into ambient mode, delivered through `AmbientLifecycleObserverBinder.bind` (installed on `MainActivity.onCreate`, via the injected `ambientBinder`) — observed.

## Today

`AlwaysOnDisplayController` is instantiated as a plain field on `MainActivity` (`val alwaysOnDisplayController = AlwaysOnDisplayController()`, not `@Inject`, not `@Singleton`), so a fresh instance is built — `mode` starting back at `DisplayMode.NORMAL` — every time the activity is recreated, a rotation included. `MainActivity` mirrors its `mode` into a local `displayMode by mutableStateOf(...)`, updates it from the `AmbientBinder` callbacks by calling `enterPowerSave()`/`exitPowerSave()`, and passes both `displayMode` and `alwaysOnDisplayController.refreshIntervalMs` down to the private `WatchApp` composable (`MainActivity.kt` lines 105-114). `WatchApp`'s parameter list declares `displayMode: DisplayMode` and `refreshIntervalMs: Long?` (lines 138-139), but its body (lines 140-226) never references either name — none of its branches (`HOME`, `MAIN`, `PROJECTION`, `CONTROL`, `END`) reads them. `MainRacePageScreen` (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/MainRacePageScreen.kt), the composable rendered for the `MAIN` destination, takes only a `viewModel: MainRacePageViewModel` parameter and has no power-save branch anywhere in its layout. `DesignTokens.Idle` (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/ui/theme/DesignTokens.kt, lines 152-166) already declares the dimmed opacities and arc widths documented as "Watch power-save variants only", but nothing in the module references `DesignTokens.Idle` — it is unused.

## Expected

`AlwaysOnDisplayController` is a Hilt `@Singleton`, injected into `MainActivity` like `ambientBinder` rather than constructed as a plain field, so its `mode` — and therefore `displayMode` and `refreshIntervalMs` — is the same value before and after a recreation, a rotation included. `WatchApp`'s `MAIN` branch passes `displayMode` and `refreshIntervalMs` on to `MainRacePageScreen` (and its `MainRacePageViewModel`), which renders its power-save layout — using the `DesignTokens.Idle` opacities and arc widths already declared for exactly this purpose — while `displayMode` is `POWER_SAVE`, and returns to its normal layout otherwise.
